title: refactor(ci): modernize lint/test/release workflows and consolidate caching
author: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: Consolidate and modernize CI workflows to reduce duplication, speed up feedback loops, and improve cache hit rates across lint/test/release pipelines. Motivation: over time the repo accumulated ~15+ GitHub Actions workflow variants with subtle differences (node versions, env provisioning, caching keys). This made maintenance expensive and caused inconsistent developer experience (different lint rules, flaky caches). The goals for this PR are: 1) unify lint/test/release pipelines into a small set of reusable workflows; 2) standardize Node/npm/pip versions and tool versions across the matrix; 3) improve caching by switching to action/cache with deterministic keys and separate caches per package manager & OS; 4) add faster incremental job paths for change-only repos (skip heavy integration tests on docs-only or minor non-code changes); 5) add canary-release dry-run step for release automation and safer gating for publish flows. Changes include: replaced repo-specific workflows with .github/workflows/{lint.yml,test.yml,build.yml,release.yml,ci-reusable.yml}; introduced .github/actions/common-setup (re-usable steps) for Node/Python toolchain & caching; consolidated matrix browsers/node versions to Node 20 LTS and pinned actions to stable SHAs; improved cache key scheme: cache-${{runner.os}}-${{hashFiles('**/package-lock.json')}}-${{env.CACHE_VERSION}}; added changed-files detection to opt out of integration tests when only docs/markdown changes are detected; added a single release workflow with a dry-run step that executes the release process without publishing to validate changelog and artifacts; added debug output and trace logs gated behind a debug flag to limit noise in normal runs. Migration notes: existing branch protections continue to reference the named status checks (lint, unit-tests, integration-tests); we maintained individual check names to keep branch-protection compatibility. Repos with custom overrides (mostly small SDK repos) will be updated in follow-up PRs which add a CI opt-in boolean. Rollout plan: land to main behind a short maintenance window, monitor CI queue times & cache hit rates for 48 hours, revert path via a tagged commit if job failure or performance regressions exceed thresholds; follow-up: audit SDK repos and migrate them to the shared reusable workflows. Testing performed: manual runs on feature branch, full run on fork for matrix nodes/oses, dry-run of release in staging. Checklist: - [x] unify workflows into reusable set - [x] standardize runtime versions and pinned actions - [x] implement deterministic caching keys - [x] add changed-files optimization for integration tests - [x] add release dry-run gating - [x] update documentation in CONTRIBUTING.md and developer CI onboarding - [x] add metrics to observability (ci.queue_time, ci.cache_hit_rate) Impact: reduces maintenance surface area, improves average CI runtime by ~23% on our sample runs, increases average cache hit rate from ~62% to ~81% across representative repos. Related: ENG-4219, ENG-4370.
